newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges release of Burma democracy activist.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges release of Burma democracy activist.

text.p: The United States on Wednesday called for the release of a democracy activist detained in Burma and urged the military authorities there to start a dialogue with the opposition on the country's future.

Kyi Maung, deputy chairman of the National League for Democracy (NLD) and a close confidant to democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi, was held for questioning on Tuesday by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).
A SLORC statement said he had met students who later took part on Wednesday in a 500-strong demonstration against the military government.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said a "very serious situation" had developed in Burma.
"We're concerned by (Kyi Maung's) detention and we believe that the Burmese government authorities should release him immediately," he told reporters.

"In addition, we're renewing today our call on the Burmese government to begin a direct dialogue with the National League for Democracy and leaders of ... ethnic minorities in Burma on the political future of Burma."

"That's a very disturbing scene to see a peaceful student demonstration turned into a situation where arrests are made (and) people are held without any kind of charge against them," Burns said. "This reflects the brutality of the Burmese government."

Burns said, however, that Washington had so far made no decision on possible further sanctions against Burma. Earlier this month, President Bill Clinton announced that senior Burmese officials would be denied entry to the United States.
